title: Tech Note: 4D Server: Networking and Troubleshooting
author: Jim Staples, Jr.

historical_commentary.text: This note is a networking primer and troubleshooting guide for 4D Client/Server connectivity in 1996, covering three protocols of that era (ADSP/AppleTalk, TCP/IP, IPX/SPX) via 4D's proprietary 'ACI Network Component' translation layer, plus the '-10002' timeout error and 4D Remote dial-up access. AppleTalk and IPX/SPX as mainstream desktop networking protocols have been discontinued for decades, and TCP/IP — the only protocol of the three still in use — is now universally built into every OS and networking stack rather than requiring a separate driver/component install, making the specific configuration steps and troubleshooting advice obsolete even though the general 'check recent changes, verify configuration, reinstall software' troubleshooting methodology remains a timeless practice.
related_updates: AppleTalk (ADSP) networking protocol was discontinued by Apple in the 2000s and is not present in any modern operating system
IPX/SPX (Novell NetWare's protocol) has likewise been discontinued and is not used in any modern networking environment
TCP/IP is universally built into every current operating system's network stack, eliminating the need for a separate 'ACI Network Component' driver/DLL installation described in this note

4D Remote, ACI's proprietary dial-up networking protocol for connecting to 4D Server without ARA, is not part of the modern 4D product line; remote access to a 4D Server today is handled via standard TCP/IP over VPN/Internet connections
